🇨🇳🇺🇸 China pauses its extra 24% tariff on US goods for another two months.

What happened: China's Customs Tariff Commission said today that it is extending the suspension of an extra 24% tariff on American imports for two more months, from 10 November. A 10% tariff stays in place. Beijing says the move follows the recent meeting between the two countries' leaders, and that it will watch what tariffs Washington uses next.

Why it matters for Mzansi: China is South Africa's biggest trading partner, and the US is a key market too. When the world's two biggest economies keep their trade fight calm, it usually helps global trade, demand for the metals and minerals we export, and confidence in emerging-market currencies like the rand. A flare-up does the opposite.

It's only two months, so watch for the next deadline in January.
